problems.title: The Challenge.
problems.closing: We don't have enough time, enough sight, or enough intelligence.

overview.title: How LOOM works.
overview.subtitle: Five integrated layers working in concert — from sensor data to rescue coordination, in under one second.

cards.title: Digital Twin Ship
cards.body: Every vessel running LOOM hosts a real-time digital mirror of its physical state. Sensors are embedded throughout the ship, tracking structural, environmental, and biological conditions simultaneously.

cards.title: Predictive Intelligence
cards.body: Real-time sensor feeds power a predictive AI engine that forecasts emergency states before they escalate, giving crews precious minutes to respond.

cards.title: Spatial Awareness
cards.body: LOOM maps the vessel's state in 3D, pinpointing critical zones and optimizing evacuation routes. The system understands every corridor, hatch, and compartment.

cards.title: Autonomous Coordination
cards.body: On distress trigger, LOOM broadcasts your exact location, vessel state, survivor count, and recommended rescue approach to all nearby surface and air assets.

cards.title: Continuous Adaptation
cards.body: As conditions evolve, LOOM recalculates rescue windows and broadcasts updated coordinates. No silent failures — crews always know the system is thinking.

cards.title: Human-in-the-Loop
cards.body: LOOM advises; humans decide. Every critical action is presented with confidence scores, alternatives, and the raw data crew members need to override.

grapnel.title: The Grapnel.
grapnel.subtitle: A modular emergency capsule for deep-ocean rescue and crew survival.
grapnel.caption: The Grapnel's reinforced hull can survive extreme pressure; the modular internal layout keeps crew comfortable during extended waits. Legroom: 55–60 cm per occupant.

modules.name: Communications
modules.description: Dual-redundant EPIRB + satphone beacon. Broadcasts distress location, survivor count, and medical status to maritime rescue authorities worldwide.

modules.name: Life Support
modules.description: Closed-loop O₂ regeneration system with 72-hour capacity for 4 occupants. CO₂ scrubbing via chemical absorption cartridges, refreshed every 8 hours.

modules.name: Medical Suite
modules.description: Integrated trauma kit, defibrillator, and basic surgical supplies. Environmental monitoring for hypoxia, decompression sickness, and thermal stress.

modules.name: Stabilization
modules.description: Vectored thrusters + active ballast tanks. Keep the capsule upright and stable during waves. Buoyancy margin: 15% above full crew load.

modules.name: Power & Control
modules.description: Redundant battery arrays (solid-state, 144 kWh total). AI core runs full diagnostics and telemetry every 5 seconds. Manual override always available.

modules.name: Comfort & Morale
modules.description: Temperature regulation (18–24°C), LED mood lighting, water supply (potable + washdown), and emergency rations. Designed for 72-hour occupancy.

showcase.title: The Fleet.
showcase.subtitle: Three capsule variants optimized for different vessel types and deployment scenarios.

technical.title: Under the Hood.
technical.subtitle: The technology that makes deep-ocean survival possible.

layers.title: Hull & Structure
layers.body: Grapnel hulls are fabricated from a titanium-steel composite, rated for 6000m depth. External pressure: 600 MPa. Interior maintained at 1 atm via active ballast. Welds inspected via ultrasonic scanning; stress-tested every 18 months.

layers.title: Atmospheric Regeneration
layers.body: Regenerative system combines sodium superoxide cartridges with electrolytic water splitting. Produces O₂ while scrubbing CO₂. Capacity: 72–120 hours depending on variant. Backup mechanical air circulation; redundant sensors monitor O₂/CO₂/N₂.

layers.title: Vectored Thruster Array
layers.body: Four hydraulic thrusters (port, starboard, bow, stern) provide full 6-axis control. Depth-pressure compensated actuators; emergency mechanical backup. Fuel: 90 minutes active maneuver time, 5 days idle station-keeping.

layers.title: Solid-State Battery Grid
layers.body: 144 kWh solid-state battery array. Supports all systems for 72–120 hours at nominal load. Solar charging via external hatch; emergency hand-crank backup. Thermal monitoring + active dissipation prevents runaway.

layers.title: Redundant Beacon Network
layers.body: Dual independent EPIRB units (121.5 MHz + 406 MHz, encrypted). Satellite link via Iridium + Inmarsat for real-time telemetry. Acoustic modem for underwater signaling. Manual distress button triggers all channels simultaneously.

about.title: Building the future of ocean rescue.
about.body: LOOM is a joint initiative between maritime safety innovators, AI researchers, and deep-sea engineering teams. Our mission: compress decades of emergency response expertise into systems that think, act, and save lives when seconds count.

grapnel_note.title: Why 'Grapnel'?
grapnel_note.body: A grapnel is a small, versatile anchor — it grips uncertain terrain and holds fast. Our capsule does the same: it grabs the ocean floor, stabilizes under pressure, and becomes a secure refuge when everything else fails.

timeline.title: First Prototype
timeline.body: Initial Grapnel-1 design validated in deep-tank simulations. Hull integrity confirmed at 3000m equivalent pressure.

timeline.title: AI Core Integration
timeline.body: Real-time predictive engine trained on 40 years of maritime incident data. System achieves 98.7% early-warning accuracy.

timeline.title: Ocean Trials
timeline.body: First sea trials off the Norwegian coast. Full 96-hour endurance test with 6 occupants. All systems nominal.

timeline.title: Regulatory Approval
timeline.body: IMO and DNV GL certification. Grapnel-1 approved for commercial maritime deployment.

timeline.title: Fleet Expansion
timeline.body: Grapnel-2 Extended and Grapnel-3 Deep variants enter production. First commercial orders from major shipping lines.

timeline.title: Global Rollout
timeline.body: 1000+ capsules deployed across international waters. LOOM AI assists in 12 active rescue operations, 11 successful.
